newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PAL workers strike, 21 flights scrapped.
newsitem.headline: PAL workers strike, 21 flights scrapped.

text.p: Workers of the Philippine Airlines (PAL) launched a crippling strike over a pay dispute on Wednesday, forcing the airline to cancel eight international and 13 domestic flights, the airline said.
Hundreds of ground crew personnel mounted pickets at Manila's domestic and international airports after President Fidel Ramos refused to intervene in the row, saying he was not a labour arbiter.

The strike by the 9,000-strong PAL Employees Association (PALEA) also delayed the departures of a Cathay Pacific Airways plane and a Qantas flight, airport sources said. PAL workers provide catering and cargo services to several foreign airlines flying to and out of Manila.

PALEA and two other unions representing pilots and cabin crew had urged Ramos to intervene to help avert a potentially embarrassing strike while the government is preparing for next month's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum summit which Ramos is hosting.
There was no indication the pilots and cabin crew unions were involved in the walkout.
"Philippine Airlines management...is saddened by the decision of the PAL Employees Association to defy the law by staging an illegal strike early tonight," the airline said in a statement.
